The new coverage came from PR #1754, "(test) Add regression tests for 401 Location-header redirect in openmrsFetch", merged 2026-05-01 under ticket O3-5629. Its author, AshThe25, opened it as a tests-only change. Reviewer ibacher asked for the branch to be cut down to just the tests, and the PR was approved on that basis. The PR body says the aim is to cover the 401-redirect path in `openmrsFetch`, which had no tests before. The commit is `e16e2d9e16a891670bbf4dd0a79ebe81414405d8`, and it only touches `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.test.ts` (63 additions, 1 deletion).

What the two new tests pin down, in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.test.ts` lines 166-214:

- **401 with a `Location` header** (lines 166-185): with `redirectAuthFailure` enabled for status 401, a configured `url` of `''`, and `resolvePromise: true`, `navigate` is called with the response's `Location` value (`/module/authentication/login.form`). This is the auth-module challenge case.
- **401 without a `Location` header** (lines 197-214): with the same config, `navigate` is called with the default login URL, the literal string `'${openmrsSpaBase}/login'`. This is the genuine auth-failure case. I did not check where that default is defined.

Together they fix the precedence the implementation uses in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.ts` lines 225-243. The target is the configured `redirectAuthFailure.url`, then the response's `Location` header, then the default. The tests use an empty configured URL, so they check the `Location` and default fallbacks. They do not check the case where a configured URL is set. A third existing test (line 216) covers a configured URL on a 401. The `Location` redirect on session-endpoint responses that the tests and code also cover was added separately in O3-5767 (commit `9dae818f0e30d56c7f31394eda770a3c15c08a8c`, PR #1797). That change is not the one that added these tests.
